SO101 arm · LeRobot · Raspberry Pi 5

SO101 Data Factory

A robot arm that collects its own training data. An LLM agent demonstrates the task, a policy trains on those demonstrations, and a fixed 31-start benchmark measures each policy.

01 · The demonstration

What one machine-made demonstration looks like

  • No human teleoperation anywhere: an LLM agent looks through the cameras, plans the motion, and drives the arm.
  • Recording runs only while the arm is moving, so every episode is one continuous trajectory with the thinking time removed.

02 · How it works

The factory loop

  • Everything on the Raspberry Pi is collection and execution; everything on the laptop is judgment and training.
  • The recorded episodes, each with a small record of what happened (start position, success, duration), are the only thing that crosses to the laptop — and a trained policy checkpoint is the only thing that comes back.
  • The loop is built to feed failures back: when the trained policy stalls, the LLM agent takes over from that exact state and the recovery is recorded as a new demonstration. This part has not been run yet.

03 · What happened

Two policies, thirty-one identical starts

  • The benchmark: 42 start positions taught by placing the arm by hand and saving the joint angles; 31 of them are the test set. Before every trial a reset tool places the roll on the marked start and verifies it by camera.
  • Success rule: the roll must land within 2 cm of the X's centre, measured on one photo. Points, order, tolerances and code are frozen in a protocol file whose hash (312efade2c) is written into every result row.
  • act_v0 and act_v1 were trained on the exact same data. The only difference: v1 predicts 150 actions per chunk instead of 100 — a longer inference time and a longer prediction horizon, about 5 s into the future instead of 3.

  • Both policies fail almost the whole inner ring and the right side of the X.
  • When either fails, the roll ends 8–24 cm out — usually dropped near the base or carried past the far edge.

04 · What this does and doesn't establish

A fair protocol, not a controlled A/B

  • Same points, order, success rule and code for both policies — every result row carries the protocol hash.
  • Not held constant: lighting (part of act_v0 ran in evening work light) and some measurement tooling fixed mid-run. The 39-vs-16 gap is larger than lighting plausibly explains; the clean test is both models interleaved in one session.
  • 31 trials per policy — enough to compare, not enough for fine-grained claims.
